event_confirmation: Company release of 2026-10-08 16:05 ET: AppFolio reports Q3 2026 after the US close on Thursday 2026-10-22, call 17:00 ET. Session amc, inside the window. Source https://finviz.com/news/400593/appfolio-inc-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-conference-call
conviction_note: Small positive lean resting on the company's own guide arithmetic (FY guide implies H2 growth of 15.4-17.4% against 19% in Q2, after three raises this year), offset by soft leasing-turnover proxies; the lean agrees with the upside-paid skew and call-heavy open interest, Q2's beat-and-raise bought only +0.67%, and the quarter's consensus is disputed between two sources, so p_up sits at 54 on a 10-point move. impact_sum (+0.6) and the scaled number (+0.8) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $294.2M from 8 analysts and EPS $1.34 (GAAP basis, 4 analysts) per https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/appf; a second aggregator snippet carries ~$298.6M, so the quarterly bar is DISPUTED and findings that depend on it are capped. FY2026: company guide $1.117-1.127B revenue, 26.5-28.0% non-GAAP operating margin (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000056/appfq22026exhibit991.htm); street FY revenue ~$1.12B (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/appf/forecast/), i.e. at the guide midpoint. Average price target $238.54, range $217-$280 (same stockanalysis page).
positioning_check: Short interest 2,441,935 shares, 7.0% of float, 8.65 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (published 2026-10-09), https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APPF/short-interest/ ; level steady at 2.2-2.7M since March 2026 (up from 1.3M in January), i.e. not building into the print but days-to-cover high because volume is thin. Baseline: 25d skew -4.4 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.17 (call-heavy, total OI only 1,145), event-implied move 12.77%, run-up +7.53% over 20 days and +0.55% over 5, spot 16% below the 52-week high. Stock rose ~24% in August, fell >10% into 1 October (Seeking Alpha 2026-10-01 per search snippet), and has recovered since.

findings.finding: AppFolio's FY2026 revenue guide ($1.117-1.127B, raised twice from an initial $1.100-1.120B) less H1 actuals ($262.0M + $281.1M = $543.1M) implies H2 revenue of $573.9-583.9M, i.e. 15.4-17.4% growth over H2 2025 ($249.35M + $248M), against 19% printed in Q2 and 20% in Q1; applying last year's Q2-to-Q3 sequential step (+5.8%) to Q2 gives ~$297M for Q3, about 1% above the $294.2M consensus, which would leave room for a fourth consecutive FY raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raises have been bought unevenly: Q2 2026 beat + raise +0.67%; Q1 2026 raise +11.16%; Q3 2025 revenue beat 1.5% + raise (EPS miss) +7.94%; Q4 2025 initial FY26 guide -8.31% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: street FY revenue (~$1.12B) sits at the guide midpoint, so a raise is the expected habit rather than a surprise, and the call-heavy open interest and negative skew show the market already leans up. What is not priced is the size of the H2 cushion: if the street had modelled a ~$297M Q3 the consensus would read ~$297M, not $294.2M. Q2 also guided to 'a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers', which the conservative H2 implies but may over-discount.
findings.independence: Initial guide and Q1 guide from the company's own releases: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1433195/000143319526000006/appfq42025exhibit991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001433195/000143319526000021/appfq12026exhibit991.htm (same issuer, so one line of evidence). Q3 2025 revenue $249.35M from https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/appfolio-appf-q3-earnings-taking-look-key-metrics-versus-estimates . The Q3 bar is disputed ($294.2M vs ~$298.6M); at $298.6M this is an in-line quarter, not a beat.

findings.finding: Apartment List's September 2026 report: national rents -0.1% m/m and -0.4% y/y, vacancy 7.0%, and units taking 34 days to lease, the slowest September since 2019, with units turning over more slowly than usual; slower leasing and turnover means fewer screenings and move-in transactions, which feed AppFolio's value-added services (78% of Q2 revenue, incl. Resident Onboarding Lift and LiveEasy move-in services management named as growth drivers).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release isolates this line; VAS growth has held at ~22% for Q1 and Q2 2026 through a flat-rent market, and the stock reacted to the headline and guide rather than to leasing activity.
findings.why_not_priced: A sector series that sell-side previews rarely tie to AppFolio's transaction revenue; if priced, Q3 estimates would sit below the seasonal run-rate rather than at ~18% growth. Proxy only: multifamily-weighted, and AppFolio skews to single-family and small multifamily.
findings.independence: Proxy. AppFolio's own Q2 remarks flagged 'a more moderate pace of unit expansion among existing customers' (https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144). Cuts against it: the broader single-family rent series is accelerating (next finding). Short interest 7% of float / 8.65 days to cover shrinks this negative.

findings.finding: Cotality's Single-Family Rent Index rose 2.0% y/y in August 2026, up from 1.8% in July and 1.5% in June, the sixth straight month of faster annual growth; with units on platform +8% y/y, rent payment volume through AppFolio Payments (the largest VAS line) would grow about 10% in Q3, a little faster than in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated in any past release; payments sits inside VAS, which grew 22% in Q1 and Q2 2026.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (August index; secondary write-up of Cotality release)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed; consensus at ~18% Q3 growth sits close to the H1 run-rate, which does not suggest an acceleration in rent volume is modelled. Small because it is a proxy and the rent effect is a few tenths of a point of revenue growth.
findings.independence: Proxy; Cotality's own press page lists the series (https://www.cotality.com/press-releases/annual-single-family-rent-strengthens-for-fourth-consecutive-month). Partly offsets the Apartment List finding; they are separate series.

findings.finding: Short interest is 2.44M shares, 7.0% of float, 8.65 days to cover (2026-09-30), held at 2.2-2.7M since March, while options open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.17) and the 25d skew is -4.4 (upside paid): a standing short that would have to cover on an above-midpoint raise, against long call holders positioned for one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest jumped 45% in February 2026 after the -8.31% initial-guide reaction and stayed; the next two prints were +11.16% and +0.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition known; what it adds is asymmetry in the reaction (thin volume, 8.65 days to cover) that the symmetric straddle does not show. Sized small because the skew already pays for upside.
findings.independence: Skew and put/call ratio from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options). Same short-interest page is the only SI source.

findings.finding: At FUTURE on 2026-09-29 AppFolio made the new Realm-X (multi-step agent, Memory, Knowledge Base, Claude connector) 'available with all AppFolio plans' and launched a Receptionist Performer, reporting AI actions up sevenfold y/y; the Q2 guide raise cited premium-tier adoption (nearly one in three units, up from one in four) as a driver, so bundling AI into every plan raises a question on the call about premium-tier upgrade pace and AI monetization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No past print reacted measurably to an AI-packaging change; Q1 2026's +11.16% coincided with Performer adoption commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: The release gives no pricing; whether bundling cannibalises premium-tier upgrades or the Performers stay paid add-ons is only answered on the call. Sign genuinely ambiguous (engagement vs monetization), hence small.
findings.independence: Premium-tier figures from the Q2 call prepared remarks: https://www.webull.com/news/15278807508870144 . Second copy of the same release: https://www.appfolio.com/newsroom/appfolio-introduces-the-new-realm-x (same document).

findings.finding: Competitor Entrata (Silver Lake-backed) filed for a US IPO in May 2026 showing Q1 2026 revenue of $143.5M, up 23% y/y, faster than AppFolio's 20%; a listed, faster-growing peer gives investors a comparison point on AppFolio's decelerating H2 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; Entrata has not priced its IPO per search results to date.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: five months old and on the wire. Filed for completeness; it matters only if the H2 deceleration is read against a faster peer on the night.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean agrees with the upside-paid skew (-4.4) and call-heavy open interest, so it is probably partly priced; the 7%-of-float short with 8.65 days to cover is the one asymmetry the straddle does not show.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 and rule 6: guidance finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0 because Q2's beat-and-raise bought only +0.67% and the quarterly bar is disputed between two aggregators.
Rule 7: Apartment List negative shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6 after checking short interest (7% of float, 8.65 days to cover); p_up moved from 55 to 54 because the lean agrees with the upside skew.
Rule 5: Cotality proxy trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4 and kept as a separate broader series beside the Apartment List proxy; both filed small.
Positioning, Realm-X and Entrata findings left standing.
